summary.motive: Use the most convincing run action in football to move an entire defense one direction, then attack the vacated half with a three-level flood.
summary.whyItWorks: Linebackers and the force safety trigger on the sweep and cannot recover, leaving the deep in isolated between a flat-watching corner and a flooded safety.
summary.failureMode: The spill-and-contain call keeps linebackers home, or the corner plays with depth instead of dropping flat, crowding the deep-in window.

beats.title: 1. The Sweep Sell
beats.text: Both guards pull exactly like Buck Sweep, the quarterback meshes with the sweeping halfback, and the entire second level starts flowing to its right.

beats.title: 2. The Waggle Boot Away
beats.text: Instead of following the sweep, the quarterback reverses out to the left behind the fullback's edge block while the defense keeps chasing the fake.

beats.title: 3. Three Levels Flooding Left
beats.text: The flood builds: the wing holds the flat, the tight end drives the crosser through the middle, and the split end climbs to the deep in.

beats.title: 4. Deep In Behind Flowed Coverage
beats.text: The waggle arrives with the deep in breaking behind a flat-dropping corner whose eyes never left the quarterback and a safety still leaning toward the sweep.

relations.tell: The quarterback reverses direction after the mesh instead of extending the handoff — live sweeps never send the ball carrier and passer to opposite halves.
